column1: # Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`qwen4_exp`) tensor census — S0 census item 4, track A deliverable.
# Plan of record: docs/investigations/qwen-flash-next-port.md   House rules: CLAUDE.md
# THIS FILE IS DERIVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. Every row below was computed from the safetensors
# HEADERS of all 131 shards (HTTP range: first 8 bytes = LE u64 header length, then that
# many bytes of JSON) plus model.safetensors.index.json, at the pinned revision. No tensor
# payload was downloaded except 282 bytes named under I64 VALUES below. Nothing here is a
# measurement of this box; it is a census of the source artifact.
# fetched at    2026-08-31T11:21:09Z  (all fetches used resolve/<sha>/<file>, never /main/)
#   Vendored because it is the ONE measured weight qwen-architecture.md overrides a primary
#   source with (T1: the tech report says zero-centred, the code and these bytes say
#   ones-centred), and a verdict whose bytes are not in tree is prose. Recomputed from this
#   file: mean +0.9667663574, min +0.875, max +1.0234375 over n=128 -- so S2 re-derives the
#   verdict rather than trusting it. The other three measured tensors are NOT vendored; their
#   shard, offsets, n and dtype are tabulated in qwen-architecture.md section T1 provenance,
#   which is enough to re-fetch them byte-for-byte.
# ---- NOT VENDORED HERE (S4 converter AUX owns the tokenizer; shas pinned for its gate) --
# tokenizer.json                12809320 B  sha256 0997f410c57a1f4e53b09e4be8f4a172d90edd9564368fb0847030937229b9f3  (LFS oid via HF tree API; only
#                              the first 8192 bytes were fetched, enough for model.type)
# ---- CENSUS CLOSURE (the assert this file exists to make checkable) ---------------------
# sum of `count` over all family rows      152089
# EQUAL: True   -- every tensor lands in exactly one family row
#   The plan's "~180 GB on disk" is the PARAMETER count, not the byte count: 180,007,507,860
#   185.50 GB. Report bytes/token budgets from the byte column, never from "180 GB" (P5).
#   Split by v1-status, re-derived from shape x count on the rows below -- these are the
#   figures the plan of record cites, so they are DECLARED here and recomputed by
#   crates/artifact/tests/qwen_names.rs rather than retyped into prose:
# ---- I64 VALUES (282 B of payload fetched; the only tensor data read) -------------------
# These are NOT hash tables. They are the n-gram HASH PARAMETERS, and they close the
# geometry of the 51.2 GB table without any further download.
#   ngram_heads_vocab_sizes  [16] = 16 distinct PRIMES just above 2e7 (all 16 verified prime)
#     three multipliers, one per position of ngram_size=3.
#     fp8 scale for the WHOLE 51.2 GB table -- NOT block-128. `Fp8W`'s block path does not
#     apply here; the n-gram gather needs a per-tensor-scale dequant. Independently
#     confirmed by upstream huggingface/transformers issue #48350, still OPEN.)
#   Closure: sum(vocab_sizes) = 320001446; the table is padded to 320001536 rows (+90) so
#   that it divides by make_ngram_vocab_size_divisible_by=128 into split_ngram_parts=128
#   shards of exactly 2500012 rows; 16 heads x 160 dims = ple_embed_dim 2560. All checked.
# v1-status   v1 | EXCLUDED-v1-MTP | EXCLUDED-v1-VISION. The EXCLUDED rows are NAMED, not
#             omitted, so the S4 converter census (item 3) can be exhaustive by name.
# name-pattern  indices collapsed: {L} layer, {E} expert, {B} vision block,
#             {S} n-gram shard. No pattern is ragged: every pattern has exactly one
#             (dtype, shape) row, so bytes-per-tensor is exact, not an average.
# Rows sorted: v1 first, then by descending total-bytes.
# The column-header row below is `#`-prefixed ON PURPOSE, so the families() parser idiom the
# k3 census already uses -- `.lines().filter(|l| !l.starts_with('#'))` then split on tabs --
# yields DATA rows only. Without the prefix that parser reaches
# `"count-of-tensors-in-family".parse::<usize>()` and panics on the first line it reads.
# The k3 contract is NOT this one (4 columns, no header row, count first), so the two
# parsers cannot yet be one function; lifting a shared helper is owed at S4, when the
# converter census gives the second reader a reason to exist
